newsitem.title: GERMANY: GOLF-A STAR IS BJORN IN HAMBURG.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-A STAR IS BJORN IN HAMBURG.

text.p: Denmark's Thomas Bjorn fired a six-under par 66 to capture a share of the lead after the third round of the Tournament Players' Championship on Saturday.
Bjorn holed six birdies on his way to the joint-best score of the day, joining Howard Clark of England and Sweden's Anders Forsbrand at the top of the leaderboard on six-under-par 210.
Former Ryder Cup stalwart Clark carded a 68 while Forsbrand hit a 69.
The trio are one stroke clear of Scotland's Gordon Brand Jnr, another Englishman, Ross McFarlane, and Ireland's Paul McGinley who also carded 66.

Overnight leader Van Phillips of England fell away with a 74 to be three shots off the pace and Spain's Miguel Martin, lost ground badly to finish six adrift despite holing birdies at the first two holes to go one ahead of the field.
European Ryder Cup captain Seve Ballesteros has called Bjorn "my Tiger Woods" when mapping out his strategy for this year's clash with the Americans in Spain.

"I'm no Tiger Woods," said Bjorn, "but it's nice to know he thinks that highly of me. I've played with him this year and he's given me a lot of encouragement. It really sounds like he wants me in the team."
Three birdies in four holes coming to the turn fired Bjorn's charge.
"I've been struggling recently but I've put in so much work I just knew something had to happen eventually," he said. "It could have been a lower score."

Lying eighth in the European Ryder Cup rankings with 276,532 points, Bjorn thinks the 83,000 points on offer for second place in Germany would be enough to seal a place in the team for the contest in Valderrama.
"I think I'm about 65,000 points away and if I can't make that by September I don't deserve to be in the team," he said.
Forsbrand birdied two of the last three holes to spring into contention. "The last time I led going into the last round, the 1995 German Masters, I won, so I'm looking forward to tomorrow," he said.
Clark's said Saturday's round was his first bogey-free card for "many moons".
